- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% of recent mean or spike magnitude.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often over-estimates continuation; cap forecast growth to 5–7% per period or apply decay factor.
- If sentiment is consistently neutral or negative (0.00), model exhibits strong mean-reversion bias; forecast should not drift below 10–15% below recent low or above 10–15% above recent high.
- Model frequently under-estimates late-period (last 5–7 days) price surges; apply a “late horizon correction” by adding 2–5% to forecast if sentiment turns positive or volatility rises.
- When sentiment history shows no recent positive signals, model tends to forecast flat or downward; if true outcome shows upward momentum, add 1–3% per period to offset lag.
- Avoid linear extrapolation; if history shows non-linear trends (e.g., sharp drop then recovery), model should not assume linear continuation; use sentiment to trigger non-linear adjustment.
